outside_dp_mechanism: StandardScaler mean and SD are fitted centrally on all training records (ppuba_lib/data.py, preprocess) without noise.
Pseudonymization, the identity-aware split, the role-based client assignment and the k-anonymity/l-diversity statistics are computed centrally on the pooled corpus before training.

Minibatches are stratified by label (up to 16 positives per batch); the dependence of the batch on the data is covered by the replace-one sensitivity 2C/B (Table D.2, replace-one columns), not by the add/remove calibration C/B.
FedAvg weights are proportional to the true client record counts (ns / ns.sum()), which are not privatized.
The training-loss curve (Figure 5.4) is computed each round on all training records without noise; it is a diagnostic output and not part of the protected release.
Decision thresholds are selected on the validation users, whose records are not protected by DP.
Noise is drawn with NumPy's PCG64 generator in floating point; no cryptographically secure RNG or protection against floating-point attacks (e.g., Mironov, 2012) is implemented.

The noise generator is seeded from the published experiment seed (seed * 7919 + int(100 eps)), so the noise is reproducible by anyone who knows the seed; this is required for reproducibility of the thesis but would remove the protection in a deployment, where the noise must come from a secret, non-reproducible source.
Protection is record-level (one user-day); a user contributes about 150 records and has no user-level guarantee.
scope: Software tests of ppuba_lib/fl.py against Table 3.4; not a formal verification or an external audit.
